newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China suppressing minority regions, Amnesty says.
newsitem.headline: China suppressing minority regions, Amnesty says.

text.p: Recent riots in China's Xinjiang province, reported to have been sparked by executions, indicated a cycle of suppression, human rights watchdog Amnesty International said on Wednesday.

"What we hear about the recent executions in Xinjiang fit a pattern of very heavy-handed response to unrest and dissent in the minority areas," Rory Mungoven, Amnesty's Asia and Pacific region programme director, told reporters.
"We see in China a deepened cycle of suppression," he said, adding that the use of the death penalty was increasing for arbitrary and political reasons.

A riot in the town of Yining in the predominantly Moslem province of Xinjiang, which left 10 people dead and about 100 hurt, was reported to have been sparked by the execution of 30 Uighurs by Chinese authorities.
Chinese authorities sealed off the town and imposed a curfew in the wake of the riot.

Although Han Chinese account for more than 90 percent of China's 1.2 billion people, Turkic-speaking Uighurs are in the majority in Xinjiang, which borders Afghanistan, Pakistan and three mainly Moslem Central Asian states.
"We've consistently raised our human rights concerns with the Chinese authorities including our concerns in Tibet and Xinjiang. We'll continue to do that," Mungoven said.
